# 3.3.2

## HTTP facade: dynamic routes for noStrict

- A `noStrict` object at facade path P is one route `<base>/P/*rest` (GET and POST mirrors alike),
  resolved on every request as RPC resolves that subtree at call time:
  `POST /api/accounts/alice/orders/add` calls `accounts['alice'].orders.add(...args)` with its owner as
  `this`. Keys added after setup work at once, and the node is never enumerated at setup. In 3.3.0-3.3.1
  HTTP skipped `noStrict` entirely; before 3.3.0 it froze the keys present at setup into routes.
- The rule is RPC's (`rcp/rpc-member.ts`): `in`, so a proxy's `has` trap decides; inherited builtin
  methods never resolve unless own; neither a function nor bytes are containers; a stream below a key
  stays unreachable. Empty or forbidden segment: 400; past `limits.maxPathLen`: 413; absent, not a
  function, builtin or stream: 404 (the message caps the echoed path). One trailing slash is ignored.
  A `noStrict` function gets no route; a `noStrict` root, or a node too deep for `maxPathLen`, is
  refused at setup.
- A route of the same method on the same app that falls below (or above) a dynamic route is refused at
  setup — one of the two could never answer.
- `routes()` entries gain `dynamic: boolean` (additive). OpenAPI documents each dynamic node as
  `<base>/P/{member}` and `<base>/P/{key}/{member}` with one-segment parameters (Swagger UI encodes a
  `/` inside a parameter); MCP serves the same node as the resource template `facade://P/{key}`.

## Security

- The builtin rule shared by RPC, MCP and HTTP also samples the platform's classes: `URL`,
  `URLSearchParams`, `AbortController`/`AbortSignal`, `EventTarget`, `Event`, `TextEncoder`/`Decoder`,
  `Headers`, `Blob`, `FormData`, `Request`/`Response`, `MessagePort`, `Buffer` (each when present).
  Before, RPC under `noStrict` resolved `URLSearchParams.delete`, `AbortController.abort` and
  `Buffer.write`.
- `isListenCallback` checks the eight Listen-core keys one by one instead of listing every key of the
  value: a dynamic request through a large array or Buffer cost up to 3 s, now milliseconds.

## Tests and docs

- Oracle `oracle/regression/http-facade-dynamic.spec.ts` (39 checks, real Express): owner as `this`, a
  key added after setup, a percent-encoded key with a slash, `has`-trap allow/deny without a get,
  builtins, bytes, streams, 400/404/413, trailing slash, overlap refusal, setup depth, the codec, the GET
  mirror, OpenAPI shapes; `rpc-nostrict-builtins` gains the platform classes. `http-facade-streams` and
  the MCP OpenAPI parity check moved to the new contract.
- Docs: rare doc *HTTP facade server* and the MCP walk, the brief MCP line, RPC-AUTH Rule 3,
  DYNAMIC-RUNTIME adapter limits.
